verdict.rationale: Pipecat is a framework for building voice agents, so plugging in MCP servers as a tool source is a fair question, but the evidence pack never documents an MCP client capability. The only MCP mention is `pipecat context-hub install`, which registers Pipecat's docs hub as an MCP server for the user's coding agent. That is the opposite, server-side role and earns no credit here. Flows functions that call external APIs are a related feature, not MCP tool consumption.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can plug MCP servers into this product so it can use their tools
